Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Mara: That makes the alternate crossing worth keeping in the plan. I checked it from the trail: the upstream section is wider and shallower, with stable gravel on the bank. We’ll only switch if the main crossing becomes unsafe; for now, nobody needs to go back and test it.

Eli: The dark grains in the creek sand are magnetic in a quick hand-magnet check, but that only tells us some grains respond to the magnet. I’ve noted the tool used and kept the observation separate from any mineral identification. Sample bag S-03 is from the dry bar surface.

Jon: I photographed the orange coating at station 14 with a ruler and a card showing the station label. The surface underneath is fractured basalt, not the grey rock from the lower exposure. I’ve put the image number beside the notebook entry so it can be found without guessing.

Mara: Lunch break at the sheltered notch. We compared notes and found one difference in the route sketch: Eli’s creek bend is about 30 meters farther south than mine. We’ll check the map grid before revising either sketch; both entries stay in the book for now.

Eli: Map check done. My mark was misplaced because I used the trail junction as the reference point instead of the creek bend. I’ve corrected the sketch with a single line through the old mark, leaving it readable, and added the grid coordinates from sheet 7B.

Jon: The cloud cover has lowered the light on the north face, so colors are harder to judge than they were this morning. The northern outcrop has visible bands, but from this safe vantage point we can’t tell whether they’re mineral layers, weathering streaks, or shadows along the slope.

Mara: We stopped short of the loose upper slope and recorded the view from firm ground. There are angular blocks below the outcrop, several with pale interiors and dark rinds. The blocks could have fallen from above, but we haven’t traced any of them to a source face.

Eli: I’ve added a notebook reminder to revisit the barometer comparison against station data before we turn these elevations into a profile. If the station’s pressure record is incomplete, we’ll report the map-based elevation only. The two readings are useful field notes, not interchangeable measurements.

Jon: End-of-day inventory: four photo sets, three filled sample bags, and one blank duplicate label returned to the kit. S-03 is the only creek-sand sample; the other two are small basalt chips from separate fresh breaks. All bags have initials and page references.

Mara: Final entry before we head back: the notebook has the route, station observations, photographs, sample references, and uncertainties from today. The creek level is still up, so we’ll take the marked trail to the higher crossing on the return.
